newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares weak at mid-session on budget fears.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares weak at mid-session on budget fears.

text.p: Indian shares were nervous at mid-session on Friday as investors saw the fate of a recently announced federal budget hang in balance, traders said.
They said fears that an ongoing political crisis would delay parliamentary approval for the 1997/98 (April-March) budget announced on February 28 had made investors nervous.
Bombay's benchmark index fell 28.48 points, or 0.80 percent, lower at 3531.17 in nervous mid-session trade.
"There is some amount of nervousness in the market due to the budget fears," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at Lloyds Securities, a local firm.

Newspapers said the budget was likely to be sidelined as the government turned its attention to the April 11 trust vote to be faced by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority coalition after its key ally the Congress party withdrew crucial support.
"The fate of the government and the fate of the budget is interlinked," a senior leader of Deve Gowda's United Front coalition, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
On the Bombay-based National Stock Exchange, the index fell 12.45 points, or 1.2 percent, to 998.30.
"Nobody's sure what's happening," said the equities head at a foreign brokerage. "There are a lot of confusing signals coming from political parties."
